label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, secret-rotation, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 6 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy webhook-receiver: WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION v2 -> v1); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.name: secret-rotation
case.title: The books stop catching up: our webhook receiver refuses every webhook
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: a deploy of the webhook receiver with a rotated secret the provider does not sign with (WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, while the provider signs with v1): every webhook fails its signature check and is refused with a 400, so no event reaches Kafka, and the provider keeps sending them again, with backoff.
case.remedy: roll the webhook receiver back to v1 (or accept both versions until the provider signs with v2): the provider sends every refused webhook again, and the books catch up by themselves

expected_symptoms: the books cannot catch up with the provider: the money check cannot settle, the provider's webhooks not acknowledged, and the books rule fires at its second evaluation, about 50 s after the deploy
the receiver refuses every webhook with a 400, counts it as bad_signature and logs 'webhook refused: bad signature'; the provider sends its growing backlog again and again, tens of times a second
nothing new is booked or confirmed, and both consumers' lag stays at 0: nothing reaches Kafka

payments and refunds still go through, but one whose answer was lost cannot be confirmed: its client's retries get 503 again, so the 5xx share of POST /payments about doubles and its p95 climbs to about 0.6 s, both under their thresholds

after the rollback the books catch up within about three minutes: the provider sends each refused webhook again within a minute of its last try, and one whose acknowledgement is then lost (the traffic's noise) a minute later
fault.remedy: roll the webhook receiver back to v1 (or accept both versions until the provider signs with v2): the provider sends every refused webhook again, and the books catch up by themselves

alert.name: BooksBehindProvider
alert.summary: Our books cannot catch up with the provider: at each of the last 2 evaluations, the money check waited 15 s and could not settle up to its cutoff. At the last one, 158 of the provider's webhooks up to it had not been acknowledged yet.

diagnosis.hypothesis: webhook-receiver was redeployed at 06:16:07 with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. Since then it rejects every provider webhook as bad_signature, so nothing is queued to Kafka and the provider keeps resending unacknowledged webhooks. The books cannot catch up, so the money check cannot settle and the alert fires. The receiver's secret most likely no longer matches the key the provider signs with. This is inferred from the timing and the bad_signature counts. I did not see the provider's signing key or the receiver's verification logic.

evidence.shows: webhook-receiver was the only service deployed after startup, at 06:16:07, with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. All other services were created at 06:14:40.

From 06:16:22 the bad_signature count climbs steeply (228 to 1556 per 5m window) while queued stays flat at about 248.571 after 06:16:22. So accepted webhooks stopped when the new receiver started and all arrivals are being rejected.
No ERROR-level logs from webhook-receiver. The rejections are counted in metrics but not logged as errors, so logs would not have revealed this.
All containers are running and healthy, with no restarts, so a crashed or stalled service does not explain the backlog.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll webhook-receiver back to its previous settings, which had the earlier webhook secret version, so signatures verify again. The provider resends unacknowledged webhooks, so the backlog should drain. Then run money_check to confirm the books settle. Afterwards, find out why v2 does not match the provider's signing secret before trying it again.

diagnosis.blast_radius: The receiver container is recreated, so webhook intake pauses briefly. The provider retries, so no events should be lost. Events already booked are unchanged, and the rollback repairs nothing. If the provider had actually moved to v2 signing, the rollback would make rejections worse.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy webhook-receiver with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2 if the rollback makes things worse. Check klaxon_webhooks_received_total by result after either change.
